Research themes

Rights need systems that can respond.

The GDPR gives people rights over their personal data. Making those rights actionable across complex data systems calls for clear responsibilities, traceable processing, and practical technical support.

01

Data subject rights

Understand how access, erasure, and portability rights can be supported through a technical framework rather than policy alone.

accesserasureportability
02

Accountable data use

Make data access and computation visible to the people and authorities who need to understand how personal data is used.

audittransparencylogs
03

Secure research

Explore how protected environments can enable analysis without exposing raw personal data to researchers or operators.

enclavesattestationminimisation

How it fits together

From a rights request to a verifiable result.

Our work investigates how secure research environments can help controllers enable analysis while keeping personal data protected and data use accountable.

01

Rights request

A person exercises a right through a controller-facing interface, with the scope of the request recorded.

dsr → request
02

Secure execution

Only approved computation runs inside an attested enclave over the minimum data required to answer the request.

enclave → compute
03

Verifiable result

Results and logs are delivered through an auditable path, without revealing raw records to the other party.

result → audit
